content.text:
Verdict: **FAIL** (lint/typecheck/build and focused tests pass, but operational migration correctness has blocking gaps).

Findings:

- `scripts/migrate.mjs:90-100` reads only `created_at` and ignores the stored migration `hash`. If an already-applied migration file is modified, startup silently skips it rather than detecting drift. This undermines committed/forward-only migration integrity and can leave production schema inconsistent with the image.
- `scripts/migrate.mjs:76-100` has no advisory/distributed lock around read/apply. Two rollout instances starting concurrently can both observe a migration as unapplied and execute it; one can fail on duplicate DDL/insert. The operations doc explicitly permits startup migration during rollout, so this race is in scope.
- `Dockerfile:24-27` runs migration as `USER node`, while `docs/operations.md` recommends a “minimally privileged application role.” The migration path requires creating the `drizzle` schema/table and applying arbitrary DDL, so a normal least-privilege runtime role will fail startup. Either separate migration credentials/role or explicitly document required privileges and a safe migration workflow.
- `scripts/migrate.mjs:29-46` validates only that the first 14 characters are digits; invalid dates normalize via `Date.UTC`, allowing malformed timestamps/collisions. It also uses timestamp alone as migration identity, so distinct directories with the same timestamp are conflated.

`.github/workflows/publish-container.yml`’s package visibility command may also be fragile for organization-owned repositories (`/user/packages/...` is user-scoped), but this is lower confidence than the migration issues.

Commands run: `bun run lint` passed; `bun run typecheck` passed; `bun run build` passed; focused migration/database-health tests passed (3 tests).
